subject: English
passage: In East Africa, chimpanzees in Gombe National Park use two different kinds of termite-fishing tools. One tool is sophisticated. The chimps modify a grass blade by stripping it and making it thin and flexible. The other tool is simple. The chimps pick up an unmodified twig from the ground. The modified grass tool is more difficult to make but is much more effective than the simple tool at extracting termites from mounds. When observing these chimpanzees, primatologist Dr. Selin Kaya found that they carry the modified tools with them as they move between termite sites, or they hide them near productive mounds. The chimps don't do the same with the simple tools. This suggests to Kaya that the ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: modified grass tools are more valuable to the chimps than the simple twig tools.
choices.B: modified grass tools are easier for most chimps to grip than the simple twig tools.
choices.C: chimps prefer to share their modified grass tools but don't share the simple twig tools.
choices.D: chimps realize that both types of tools are less effective than their fingers at extracting termites from mounds.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it most logically completes the text's discussion of the two types of termite-fishing tools used by chimpanzees at Gombe. The text indicates that the more effective type of tool is a grass blade that the chimps modify themselves, while the other type of tool is simply a twig that the chimps find and don't modify in any way. According to the text, Kaya found that the chimps carry modified tools with them or hide them near productive sites—but not the simple tools—when they aren't using the tools. If the modified tools are more effective than the simple tools are and the chimps are more protective of the modified tools than they are of the simple tools, it's reasonable to conclude that the modified tools are more valuable to the chimps than the simple tools are.
